meta.title: 3D Bioprinting Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Neural Tissues Using a Fibrin-Based Bioink.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells were bioprinted in the lab's fibrin-based bioink on the RX1 printer and differentiated toward dopaminergic neurons for 12 days. Cells expressed TH and TUJ1 and released dopamine.

formulations.crosslinking: CaCl2 + chitosan + thrombin crosslinker, co-extruded in microfluidic printhead
formulations.review_notes: Pressure converted from 50 mbar (bioink channel). Viability is reported in figures; no single number in the text.
formulations.name: Fibrin bioink (MSC to dopaminergic neurons)
formulations.composition_detail: 20 mg/mL fibrinogen, 0.5% w/v alginate, 0.3 mg/mL genipin
formulations.cell_type: mesenchymal stem cells differentiated to dopaminergic neurons
formulations.key_outcome: Printed MSCs expressed TH and TUJ1 after 12 days of dopaminergic induction.

evidence.quote: The final concentration in the bioink for fibrinogen, sodium alginate, and genipin was 20 mg/mL, 0.5% w/v, and 0.3 mg/mL, respectively.
The MSCs were then thawed and mixed with the bioink at a concentration of 2 × 106 per 1 mL of bioink.
The pressure of the crosslinker, bioink and buffer were 60 mbar, 50 mbar, and 100 mbar, respectively.
the elastic modulus was around 1 kPa, which is the optimal stiffness for neuronal differentiation
